execution_evidence.detail: Primary-observation resolution (executor-flagged anomaly): the 400 TRACED TO THE RANGE-INDEX PRECONDITION, not to rejection of the heterogeneous/mixed batch. The triggering log contains exactly ONE request (M1); the script returns immediately after M1's 400 (script lines 218-223), so M2/M3 never ran and no other leg in this log can carry the mixed-promise violation. The script's setup() (debate_logs/boundary_points_query_batch_mixed_008.py lines 144-158) seeds payload {grp, rank} with NO payload-index creation anywhere (no PUT /collections/{coll}/index call), while M1's searches[1] is {"query": {"order_by": {"key": "rank", "direction": "asc"}}, "limit": 3} — a documented precondition the script never established. claim_alignment=partial: the M1 REQ/RESP is exactly the claimed observation (heterogeneous batch -> 400), but the claim's defect mechanism (unjustified rejection violating the 'execute multiple universal queries in one call' promise) is contradicted by the error body and by the comparative legs (a non-heterogeneous valid batch failed identically; a heterogeneous batch with a satisfied order_by precondition succeeded per-entry with 200). What reproduced stably across scripts is the precondition-400 pattern, not a heterogeneity rejection. Multi-script grade A reflects that mechanical reproduction, not defect strength.

Within its domain the promise is honored: mixed_variant_004's heterogeneous [nearest, order_by desc, nearest] batch returned 200 with per-entry results including a working order_by entry. The constraint citation itself is the right one (it is the constraint the script declared, script line 11).

chain_trace.break_detail: The log's DEFECT_FOUND verdict attributes the 400 to the heterogeneous-batch promise ('endpoint promise: execute multiple universal queries in one call'), but the raw response body attributes it to the order_by range-index precondition — a script-side fixture gap (no PUT /collections/{coll}/index anywhere in the script), mirroring the rubric's 'judged DEFECT_FOUND but the raw response shows the target already rejected [an invalid request]'. Comparative forensics prove the attribution wrong: (1) a valid non-heterogeneous documented batch failed with the byte-identical error on the same key 'rank' (positive_001 B1); (2) the single-query face failed identically on key 'ts' (variant_matrix M5) — the check is per-query, not batch-level; (3) a heterogeneous batch whose order_by entry had a satisfied precondition returned 200 with per-entry attribution (mixed_variant_004, NO_DEFECT); (4) the source hard-requires a numeric index for order_by with an explicit instructive error and the maintainer's own test creates the integer index before any order_by use (tests/consensus_tests/test_order_by.py:17-20). The primary observation is a script-precondition failure, not a defect of the endpoint.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix query_points_batch (src/actix/api/query_api.rs:110; destructures QueryRequestBatch{searches} and iterates entries one by one — no homogeneity constraint across entries) -> Collection::query_batch (lib/collection/src/collection/query.rs:445; takes Vec<(CollectionQueryRequest, ShardSelectorInternal)>, resolves referenced vectors, executes concurrently, returns Vec<Vec<ScoredPoint>> — one result per entry) -> shard/segment execution -> SegmentReadView::filtered_read_by_index_ordered (order_by.rs:36-41) / filtered_read_by_value_stream (order_by.rs:109-114): payload_index.numeric_index_for(&order_by.key).ok_or_else(MissingRangeIndexForOrderBy) — hard requirement, no un-indexed fallback -> OperationError::MissingRangeIndexForOrderBy (operation_error.rs:61-64; error text itself instructs 'Please create one to use `order_by`' and links the official indexing doc) -> CollectionError::bad_input (types.rs:1147) -> HTTP 400 for the whole batch (fail-fast).
source_grounding.detail: The order_by range-index requirement is explicitly intentional in source: the error string itself is a maintainer instruction ('Please create one to use `order_by`. Check https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/indexing/#payload-index') and the maintainer's own integration test creates the integer payload index before any order_by use (tests/consensus_tests/test_order_by.py:17-20). Batch heterogeneity itself is fully supported: the actix handler and Collection::query_batch convert and execute each searches[] entry independently, and the behavioral leg mixed_variant_004 confirms a heterogeneous [nearest, order_by desc, nearest] batch returning 200 per-entry. Therefore neither 'validation_absent' nor a promise violation holds; the observed 400 is the designed enforcement of a documented precondition that the attacking script never satisfied (its setup creates payload key 'rank' with no index).
